clue.text: Student's joint award?

parts.note: a student is a scholar, and the possessive keeps its S
the hip is a joint of the body

explanation.surface: A prize shared jointly between two pupils.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joint award' reads as a prize shared by two, but the clue splits as 'Student's joint' (a scholar's hip) followed by the definition 'award'.
explanation.definitionFit: A scholarship is a grant of money awarded to a student for study.

clue.text: Accommodation that may be allocated to maestro

indicators.note: letters allocated afresh are dealt out into a new order, so the words to maestro are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cabin on a ship might be assigned to a visiting conductor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'allocated' rearranges TOMAESTRO into the nine-letter answer; 'that may be' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: A stateroom is a private cabin on a ship, a form of lodging aboard.

clue.text: Flexible border arrangement that's in fashion

definitions.text: Flexible border arrangement that's in fashion

parts.words: Flexible border arrangement that's in fashion
parts.note: the edge of a skirt or dress whose height moves up and down as styles change, so it is a flexible border set by fashion

explanation.surface: A garden edging layout that happens to be trendy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'border' suggests a flower bed, but it is the bottom edge of a garment, raised or lowered according to the fashion of the day.
explanation.definitionFit: A hemline is the level of a skirt's lower edge, which rises and falls with changing styles.

clue.text: City that could be right over the water?

definitions.text: City that could be right over the water?

parts.words: City that could be right over the water?
parts.note: a down-clue picture: the organ found on the body's right side sitting over a body of water spells a port city on the Mersey

explanation.surface: A town that might sit just across a river.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry the organ on the right side of the body (LIVER) stands over POOL (the water). The city, a port in north-west England, also faces the Wirral across the River Mersey.
explanation.definitionFit: Liverpool is a major English port city on the estuary of the River Mersey.

clue.text: Carpets covering new steps

indicators.note: the carpets lie over the next letter, so that word surrounds it

parts.note: rugs are small carpets

explanation.surface: New stair carpet laid over the steps.
explanation.definitionFit: Rungs are the crossbars of a ladder, the footholds you climb on.

clue.text: Did he have close ties in the entertainment business?

definitions.text: Did he have close ties in the entertainment business?

parts.words: Did he have close ties in the entertainment business?
parts.note: close ties suggests intimate connections, but here it means being tightly bound with ropes and chains as part of a stage act

explanation.surface: Asking whether some showman was well connected in show business.
explanation.walkthrough: 'close ties' sounds like friendships in the industry; it means the tight bonds a famous escapologist had to wriggle out of on stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Harry Houdini was the celebrated escape artist who freed himself from chains, ropes and locks before audiences.

clue.text: Edge in very quietly and dress

indicators.note: the edge word is placed inside the musical marking for very quiet

parts.note: pp (pianissimo) is the musical direction for very quietly
a rim is an edge

explanation.surface: Sidling in silently and getting dressed.
explanation.definitionFit: To primp is to groom or smarten oneself fussily, as when dressing up.

clue.text: Cornwall is to supply weapons to the mob

parts.note: Cornwall is in the South West of England, abbreviated SW
to arm is to supply with weapons

explanation.surface: The Cornish region plans to hand out guns to a gang.
explanation.walkthrough: Cornwall is the county at England's south-western tip, hence SW.
explanation.definitionFit: A swarm is a large, disorderly crowd, just as a mob is.

clue.text: Arrange for run after the theatre

indicators.note: the word for run comes after the word for the theatre

parts.note: the stage stands for the theatre as a profession
to run a business is to manage it

explanation.surface: Organising to dash off once the play has finished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'run after the theatre' suggests hurrying out once a show ends; 'after' is a placing instruction and 'for' only links the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: To stage-manage is to organise or orchestrate events behind the scenes.

clue.text: Given turn, making a guess!

annotationWithheld.why: Given turn, making a guess! (9): the anagram of GIVEN TURN needs 'making' as its indicator, but the definition 'making a guess' also needs it (VENTURING does not mean 'a guess'), so one word does two jobs

clue.text: Depart angry, upset at the airy gathering

indicators.note: upset means knocked over, so the letters of depart angry are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone storms off in a temper from an outdoor party.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden party is a social event held outdoors, in the open air.

clue.text: A phone that's right in the loft

parts.note: TEL is the abbreviation for telephone
i.e. (id est) means that is

explanation.surface: There is a telephone just right up in the attic.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's studio, often a light room at the top of a building, much like a loft studio.

clue.text: Smoked fish on Sunday, captain?

indicators.note: in an across clue, the fish placed on Sunday means it follows that letter

parts.note: a kipper is a smoked herring

explanation.surface: Is the captain having smoked herring for Sunday breakfast?
explanation.walkthrough: A kipper is a split, smoked herring, a traditional British breakfast.
explanation.definitionFit: A skipper is the master of a ship or leader of a team.

clue.text: Remember fine incurred during the previous night

indicators.note: the word for fine is taken in during the evening before, sitting inside it

parts.note: eve is the evening before an event
OK means fine

explanation.surface: Recalling a penalty picked up the night before.
explanation.definitionFit: To evoke is to call something to mind, bringing a memory back.

clue.text: Stubborn old boys with money to eat out

parts.note: OB is short for old boy, so old boys gives OBS
tin is slang for money
ate is the past tense of eat

explanation.surface: Unyielding former pupils with cash go out to dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with', 'to' and 'out' are linking; OB is a British term for a former pupil of a school.
explanation.definitionFit: Obstinate means stubbornly refusing to change one's mind.

clue.text: A brief salutation via radio

parts.note: brief means short
a wave of the hand is a greeting

explanation.surface: A quick hello sent over the airwaves.
explanation.definitionFit: Shortwave is a band of radio frequencies used for long-distance broadcasting.

clue.text: Blast area for sculpting stone

indicators.note: sculpting reshapes material, so the letters of blast area are reshaped

explanation.surface: Blasting a quarry site to obtain carving stone.
explanation.definitionFit: Alabaster is a soft, translucent mineral, often carved into ornaments.

clue.text: A right crazy sick old creature

parts.note: mad means crazy
ill means sick

explanation.surface: A thoroughly deranged, ailing elderly animal.
explanation.definitionFit: The armadillo is an armoured mammal of the Americas.

clue.text: Dearly loved doctor accepts a fish

indicators.note: the doctor takes the letter a inside, accepting it

parts.note: ling is a sea fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A beloved medic takes in a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: A darling is someone cherished, much beloved.

clue.text: Perhaps crawled quietly into the waterlogged ground?

parts.note: the crawl is a swimming stroke, so crawled is one way of having swum
p (piano) means quietly in music

explanation.surface: Did someone creep silently into the boggy land?
explanation.walkthrough: 'crawled' suggests creeping on hands and knees; here it is the front crawl stroke, so 'Perhaps crawled' gives SWAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A swamp is marshy land saturated with water.

clue.text: The pay? It's up, and the writer began drinking!

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means the letters of it's are read from the bottom

parts.note: a pen is a writing instrument

indicators.note: began picks out the beginning letter of drinking

explanation.surface: Salary has gone up, so the author has started on the booze.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns ITS into STI; 'began' takes D, the first letter of 'drinking'.
explanation.definitionFit: A stipend is a fixed regular salary or allowance, as paid to clergy.

clue.text: Notice part of chapter is unfavourable

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a newspaper
a verse is a numbered part of a chapter of the Bible

explanation.surface: A paragraph in a book's section proves unwelcome.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverse means harmful or contrary to one's interests.

clue.text: Five-nil. Almost call it too loud

parts.note: V is the Roman numeral for five
nil means nothing, the letter O

indicators.note: almost the whole word call, losing its final letter

explanation.surface: A five-nil scoreline: almost too noisy to call.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' and 'too' are linking; 'Almost' trims CALL to CAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Vocal means outspoken and noisily insistent.

clue.text: The compiler gets up, sick of finding the post!

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting up means the word for the compiler is read upwards

parts.note: the setter of a crossword refers to themselves as me
to ail is to be sick

explanation.surface: The setter gets out of bed, fed up of finding the mail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gets up' turns ME into EM; 'of finding' is linking.
explanation.definitionFit: Email is electronic mail, the modern equivalent of letters delivered by mail.

clue.text: Where an unsatisfactory tune might vanish?

definitions.text: Where an unsatisfactory tune might vanish?

parts.note: thin means feeble or unsatisfactory, as a thin excuse
an air is a tune

explanation.surface: Asking where a poor melody might disappear to.
explanation.definitionFit: To vanish into thin air is to disappear without trace.

clue.text: Deal with china cooking food in Mexico

indicators.note: cooking means doctoring, so the letters of deal and china are mixed

explanation.surface: Coping with crockery while cooking Mexican food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the two pieces of fodder and gives no letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An enchilada is a Mexican dish of a tortilla rolled round a filling.

clue.text: Have a go after two points give admission

indicators.note: the word for have a go comes after the two compass points

parts.note: E and N are two compass points
to try is to have a go

explanation.surface: Attempt it once you have two points to gain entrance.
explanation.definitionFit: Entry is the right or act of going in, the same as being let in.

clue.text: Cash offer that's within the law

parts.note: legal means lawful
to tender is to offer, and a tender is an offer

explanation.surface: A cash bid that is lawful.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that's' is linking; the pieces come in answer order although the clue gives them the other way round.
explanation.definitionFit: Legal tender is money that must by law be accepted in payment.
